LATIN TIMES: Mexico Homicides Plunge to Historic Lows During 2026 World Cup Opening Days
June 19, 2026 | 🟢

📰 30 homicides the day Mexico played South Africa. 27 the following week. Down from 70+ per day at the start of Sheinbaum's term. Latin Times calls it "the Sheinbaum Effect."

Rare US-facing coverage that lets the numbers speak — no obligatory cartel paragraph for balance, no "but experts caution." Compare to the NYT's and WSJ's silence on the same data.

• "Mexico Homicides Plunge to Historic Lows"
• "the Sheinbaum Effect"
• 70+/day in Oct 2024 → 30/day during World Cup opener

NATIONAL REVIEW: Claudia Sheinbaum Leads Mexico into Confrontation
June 17, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Joshua Treviño (Texas Public Policy Foundation) argues Sheinbaum has put Mexico "on a collision course with both the United States and with basic Mexican democratic civics."

The opener invokes "April 19 deaths of two CIA officers in Chihuahua" — never officially acknowledged by Washington — as the precipitating crisis. The word "regime" does the rest of the work.

• "her government is on a collision course with both the United States and with basic Mexican democratic civics"
• "Mexico's regime is dragging it toward the abyss"
• "the damage done will take a generation to repair"

WSJ: Mexico Is Starting to Push Back Against Trump's Pressure Campaign
June 22, 2026 | 🟡

📰 WSJ confirms what Sheinbaum has been saying for months: Trump pressed her on a phone call to accept "a bigger role for the U.S. military" against cartels. She refused.

The headline almost reads as praise — until you notice the framing treats Mexican sovereignty as a "hardline stance" rather than the default position of any independent state.

• "Sheinbaum's hardline stance signaled that U.S. pressure for unilateral military intervention would put her and Trump on a collision course"
• Mexico refused to extradite indicted governor Rubén Rocha Moya
• 269 Mexican extradition requests still pending in US courts

NYT: No End in Sight for U.S. Military Mission Along Border
June 20, 2026 | 🟡

📰 9,000 active-duty troops still parked at the border at $525M for the first four months — and the NYT itself admits Trump's "goal of slashing illegal crossings" was already met months ago.

The piece quietly notes Mexican soldiers are doing joint patrols. The cartel rationale stays useful long after the migration pretext expired.

• "tens of millions of dollars each week"
• "Our service members did not sign up for immigration enforcement" — Rep. Sara Jacobs
• "We remain focused on the mission of sealing the border" — Maj. Gen. David Gardner

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICAN INFLATION DROPS TO 3.94% — BACK INSIDE BANXICO'S TARGET RANGE</u>

Annual inflation cooled to 3.94% in May, down from 4.45% in April — the lowest reading in four months and back inside Banxico's ±1pp variability band around its 3% target, INEGI data shows. Non-core inflation collapsed from 5.08% to 3.10% on the back of moderating agricultural prices; core eased to 4.19%, its lowest since May 2025.

That gives Banxico room to keep its rate parked at 6.50% — the midpoint of its neutral range — while still claiming a credible path to 3% by Q2 2027. Mexico's monetary policy still works the boring way: data first, theatrics never.

Source: El Economista

🇲🇽🏭 <u>BRUGADA DOUBLES IZTAPALAPA'S FLOOD-CONTROL CAPACITY — 200 TO 400 MILLION LITERS</u>

CDMX delivered the rehabilitated Vaso Regulador El Salado yesterday in Iztapalapa: 96 million pesos invested, 80,000 cubic meters of sediment removed, perimeter levees raised 1.5 meters. Storage capacity doubled from 200 to 400 million liters — the equivalent of 160 Olympic pools.

It's one piece of a 427-million-peso flood-mitigation plan for the city's east: new pumping plants, the República Federal collector, and eight storm tanks along Calzada Ignacio Zaragoza. Iztapalapa floods every rainy season under aquifer-overexploitation cracks and subsidence. The 4T quietly builds the public works neoliberalism wouldn't.

Source: El Soberano

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MORENA OPENS CANDIDATE REGISTRATION TODAY — BANS NEPOTISM AND EXCESS SPENDING. ALLIES PT AND PVEM SKIP THE RULES</u>

The June 22-27 registration window opens today at the WTC in Mexico City. Morena requires its aspirants to step down from public office before competing, caps campaign spending, and bars nepotism. PT and PVEM — its coalition partners — face none of those internal rules.

Citlalli Hernández, Morena's elections chief, owned the asymmetry on the record: "Es una regla que tiene Morena, que no necesariamente tienen nuestros partidos aliados." One ruling party disciplining itself in public while the others ride the coattails. That's the cost of holding the alliance.

Source: Contralínea

🇲🇽🌎 <u>SHEINBAUM TO RECEIVE FELIPE VI THIS THURSDAY — AGENDA: PUEBLOS ORIGINARIOS, AMLO'S 2019 LETTER STILL UNANSWERED</u>

Felipe VI lands in Mexico June 25 ahead of Spain's World Cup match in Zapopan. Sheinbaum confirmed the meeting will focus on indigenous peoples — "su importancia en México a lo largo de la historia antes de que llegaran los españoles a ahora."

On AMLO's still-pending 2019 letter requesting a formal apology for Conquest atrocities, she didn't fold: "Si bien no es el perdón que se solicitó en su momento, sí es un avance." The Crown can attend an indigenous-women exhibition. The apology stays open.

Source: Contralínea

🇲🇽🏭 <u>FONDO DE PENSIONES BIENESTAR: 7,244 RETIREES NOW GET 96.1% OF THEIR LAST SALARY — UP FROM 52.5%</u>

In two years of operation, AMLO's Fondo de Pensiones para el Bienestar has lifted 7,244 retirees from 52.5% to 96.1% of their final paycheck — an average bump of 4,820 pesos per month, with beneficiaries pulling in 17,885 pesos monthly, IMSS pension chief Humberto Vázquez confirmed.

The payout adjusts for inflation every year. State recovering — quietly, retiree by retiree — what neoliberal Afore privatization stole.

Source: La Jornada

🚨🇲🇽 <u>CDMX IS THE NEW DREAM — NOT THE US — FOR MIGRANT CARAVANS</u>

The third migrant caravan of the year just left Tapachula. They named it "De la Mano de Dios" — and like the 18 caravans before it under Sheinbaum's administration, it's not heading to the US border. It's aiming for Mexico City, Guadalajara, and Monterrey, where migrants say there are "más y mejores" job options.

Trump can build all the walls he wants. Migrants stopped trying to cross. The dream relocated.

Source: La Jornada
